23620: Despite the intense exploitation of ornamental fish species in the Rio Negro for several decades, basic biological parameters, mainly the genetic structure of the populations and their renewal capability, are poorly known. Knowledge of the genetic diversity of an organism is one of the crucial aspects to be known for both basic and applied conservation purposes. To help in the development of a management strategy of ornamental fish in the Rio Negro we performed a fish genetic study, including cytogenetics (chromosomal analyses by conventional staining methods) and molecular biology (sequencing of ND4L/ND4 mtDNA genes, and an intron of growth homone) on three Amazonian ornamental fish species: the cardinal tetra (Paracheirodon axelrodi), the black-winged (Carnegiella marthae) and the marbled hatchet fishes (Carnegiella strigata). The species were sampled in the tribuataries of left and right margins of the Rio Negro (Amazon Basin) in a transect of about 600 Km. Karyotypes, dendograms and statistical analysis of the data generated by this study provided estimates of genetic diversity and evolutionary relationship among sampled populations. These findings are discussed with respect to the future strategies for the management of these fish species taking into account mixing populations, genetic variation, and conservation priorities issues. We expect to lay out a framework that may serve as a proposal for using our current background to study the genetic structure of ornamental fish in the Rio Negro Basin by means of chromosome, mtDNA and nDNA markers.

23621: We hereby provide a unique fieldwork method for fast, easy and minimal invasive DNA sampling, appropriate for endangered vertebrate species. Our method has been successfully tested on representatives of Testudinidae, Ranidae, Salamandridae and Muridae. This simple technique avoids harmful injuries of protected animals. Standard extraction methods yield DNA of adequate amount and quality for PCR procedures. Our method offers a versatile tool for population monitoring with regard to conservation genetics. It was employed in our studies comparing the population structure and genetic diversity of selected Emys orbicularis populations from Germany, Poland and Spain.

23622: The fish assemblages of the Mamoré River floodplain (Bolivia) were surveyed in eight lakes situated on an environmental gradient related to the river distance: lakes situated near the river, in the forested floodplain, at the floodplain edge and lakes isolated in the savanna. The diet analysis of 71 species (among the 140 recorded) conducted to determine five trophic guilds: algivores/iliophages, herbivores, zooplanktivores, invertivores and piscivores. The taxonomic and trophic structures of the fish assemblages were not similar in the different lakes of the Mamoré. The trophic structure showed a coarse pattern of dominance of algivores/iliophages and invertivores, but different relative abundance of the trophic groups were observed in relation to the spatial position of the lakes. Lakes close to the river appeared more favorable to the microphages (algivores/iliophages, zooplanktivores) although remote lakes appeared more favorable to the macrophages (invertivores, herbivores). Piscivores were equally present in all the lakes.
23623: Based on previous information that only 10 % of eggs are fertilized in foam nests of Leptodactylus labyrinthicus, and are consumed by the tadpoles, we decided to confirm the information and tested the influence of the ingestion of trophic eggs on the survivorship and growth of tadpoles. To verify growth, tadpoles were divided into two groups: Treatment I, reared in foam nest with trophic eggs, and subsequently fed on fish dry food (ad libitum); Treatment II, reared in water and fed only on fish dry food (ad libitum). Body length of larvae was measured at intervals of ca. 5 days, and snout-vent length (SVL) and body weight of metamorphosed specimens were registered. Such experiment was repeated with three different clutches. To verify survivorship, groups of tadpoles were reared in foam nests with trophic eggs and without additional food, which was repeated with two different clutches. Foam nests contained an average of 2756 ± 821 eggs (N = 4; range = 1817-3786), and mean percentage of fertilized eggs was 6.5% ± 3.1 (N = 5; range = 3.4-11.5%). Individuals from Treatment I grew better than those in Treatment II, and were larger (t = 3.6; p = 0.0006) and heavier (t = 3.5; p = 0.001) by the end of metamorphosis. Tadpoles reared in foam nests without additional food diminished in size, decreased development, but could survive ca. 40 days in the first experiment, and ca. 70 days in the second. One tadpole had metamorphosed with a small size. Our results confirm occurrence of trophic eggs in foam nests of L. labyrinthicus, and suggest that this phenomenon may be important for the maintenance of tadpoles in unpredictable environments regarding rainfall, where this species occurs.

23624: Although rare, some anuran species are known to show multi-male spawning, and multiple paternity and testes size positively related to sperm competition have been demonstrated. We report the occurrence of multi-male spawning in Leptodactylus chaquensis and L. podicipinus, and compare relative testes mass of leptodactylids to species in other 4 families (Bufonidae, Hylidae, Ranidae, and Rhacophoridae). Observations were made in the Pantanal, municipality of Corumbá (19° 34' S; 57° 00' W), Mato Grosso do Sul State, Brazil. Field observations of mating behavior of L. chaquensis and L. podicipinus were made from Oct/2000 to Apr/2001. Body and testes mass of leptodactylids (2 genera, 11 species), collected in the Pantanal or housed in collections, were determined on electronic balances. In four other foam nests we observed large males calling in the center of the nest surrounded by males; male-male combats were recorded in three nests but pair formations or multi-male spawning behavior were not observed. 23625: Many vertebrates respond to novel situations with a hormonal stress response, specifically the release of corticosteroids from the adrenal glands. In light of evidence demonstrating a negative effect of corticosteroids on mammalian embryos we wanted to determine whether pregnant female lizards have an adrenal gland response (release of corticosterone) when stimulated by the pituitary hormone ACTH (adrenocorticotropic hormone), and whether a pulse of corticosterone during pregnancy has a negative effect on the outcome of pregnancy or on the fitness of the offspring. Female common geckos (Hoplodactylus maculatus) pregnant with two offspring (stages 34-39) were collected from Central Otago, New Zealand. Control and experimental animals received an intraperitoneal injection of saline or ACTH (0.45 ug/g body weight) respectively. Geckos were retained in the laboratory until parturition. Size at birth, sprint speed, and growth were measured for all offspring. Corticosterone assays on blood taken immediately prior to and 1 hr following saline or ACTH injection indicated that pregnant females responded to ACTH by releasing corticosterone. On average, ACTH caused corticosterone levels to increase 8- fold above resting levels, whereas saline caused corticosterone levels to increase only 2-fold. Eighty and 90% of the control and experimental females respectively delivered 1-2 offspring. There were no significant differences between treatment groups in the duration of gestation or the total mass of offspring produced by each female. Similarly, offspring did not differ between treatments in mean mass at birth, sprint speed on the day after birth, or growth in mass or length over the first 30 days after birth. Despite the very high plasma corticosterone concentration achieved as a result of ACTH injection (approximately 4 times higher than the peak concentration reached as a result of handling stress) there were no significant effects on the aspects of offspring quality measured. Thus, a short period of exposure to elevated maternal cortocosteroids is not obviously harmful to embryos. This supports concurrent research in which we show that common geckos do not suppress the hormonal stress response to capture during pregnancy.

23626: The diversity and distribution of Pacific iguanas were altered drastically following human colonization around 2800 years ago. 23627: An estimated 130 fish species were identified from 12,680 specimens collected throughout the Aro River basin (Venezuelan Guyana Shield). 23632: Digestive physiology in larval anurans is a relatively unstudied area of biology. 23634: In recent years, reproductive impairment and population declines have been reported for American alligators (Alligator mississippiensis) inhabiting contaminated lakes in Florida, USA, increasing concerns over the impacts of environmental pollution on crocodilians worldwide. 23636: While some of the well-known studies done on fish that address species formation and adaptive radiation have been done on the freshwater cichlids of Africa; patterns from freshwater systems are of limited applicability to the more open population systems of closely related species in marine environments. Thus the dynamics of how historical biogeography and gene flow maintain species boundaries between closely related marine fish species is still at best poorly understood. Preliminary results indicate that several of these sculpins have some degrees of population structure and phylogenetic breaks in the Los Angeles and Oregon region. The intraspecific relationships of each genus are analogous which could perhaps be due to similar selection forces (i.e. population extinction's and range expansions) on both groups therefore resulting in similar phylogenetic histories, which could imply that each genus has had similar evolutionary histories. The nuclear markers up to this point are inconclusive and further results will be presented at the meeting. The results of this study will help assist reserve managers in marine reserve design as well as to continue to maintain suitable habitat for intertidal fish. 23638: The caecilian Dermophis mexicanus maintains body posture and generates forward force during burrowing with a hydrostatic skeleton. 23641: Despite increasing attention to the ecology of snakes in recent years, the majority of snake species remain relatively poorly known. 23644: Loricariidae is the largest catfish family with 686 species currently recognized. 23645: Nearshore Aleutian Island ecosystems have recently undergone radical changes as otter populations have declined by an order of magnitude over the past decade; as a result, sea urchin densities and biomasses have increased, and kelp densities have decreased. I used this recent collapse of sea otters and kelp forests to better document the potential radiating trophic relationship between sea otters and kelp forest fish. Variation in fish diversity increased across islands from 1986 to 2000, and was thus less tightly correlated with sea otter densities. This increase in fish diversity may result from other top down or bottom up forcing mechanisms. Changes in rock greenling stomach contents appear to be at least partially correlated with kelp densities. These findings suggest that trophic radiations occur in this system, and that trophic linkages occur across several species and species groups.

23646: Amphibians in nature face heterogeneous predator and competitor environments. In response to this heterogeneity, many amphibians have evolved phenotypically plastic traits. We studied the movements, habitat use, and diet of long-necked turtles (Chelodina longicollis) in a rice agroecosystem in southeastern Australia during 2001-2002. The turtles' pattern of habitat use supported our hypothesis that the rice agroecosystem serves as a surrogate for natural wetlands for C. longicollis. Turtles spent much of the year in the more permanent irrigation channels, but quickly moved (over land or by feeder channels) into seasonally-available flooded rice paddies, where they remained for up to six months. However, our prey sampling found no evidence for higher richness and abundance of prey in rice paddies, although the greater dispersion promoted by rice paddies may translate into higher prey productivity per turtle. Our diet data indicate that C. longicollis became more selective as prey availability increased, refuting past inferences to the generalistic dietary habits of the species, but in accordance with optimal foraging theory.

23648: Leptodactylus pentadactylus has an extensive distribution range; it is found from Honduras south through coastal Pacific Colombia and adjacent Ecuador and the greater Amazon Basin. Anuran species with extensive distribution ranges have the potential to exhibit variable degrees of genetic diversification due to local adaptation and/or isolation. However, in some cases genetic diversification may not be correlated with morphological differentiation as evidenced in other Leptodactylus species (e.g., sibling species Leptodactylus mystaceus and L. didymus). Herein we test the hypothesis that L. pentadactylus is a single species or a complex of species. Leptodactylus knudseni, labyrinthicus, and pentadactylus are part of a monophyletic clade characterized, in part, by a facultatively or obligatory carnivorous tadpole. Genetic diversity of L. pentadactylus was assessed using 12s mitochondrial ribosomal DNA sequences. Samples were obtained from populations throughout its range from Honduras, Panama, Ecuador, Peru and Brazil (eastern and western populations). Sequence data were also collected for L. knudseni and L. labyrinthicus. We obtained approximately 900 base pairs for each individual sample, of which 800 bp were unambiguously aligned using Clustal X and analyzed using PAUP*. The sequence data indicate that there is considerable genetic differentiation among the samples of L. pentadactylus that ranges between 0.12% and 10%. These preliminary results suggest that there may be 4-5 species hidden under the nominal taxa L. pentadactylus.

23649: The fish species Prochilodus lineatus is endemic to the Paraná-Paraguay River basin in south part of South America where has a considerable economical importance. Available data indicate that landings of P. lineatus in the Paraná River over the last twelve years have significant decreased mainly due to the presence of numerous hydroelectric plants and dams. These dams are formidable barriers to dispersal of migratory species such as P. lineatus, and may have disrupted, with negative impacts, the historical population structure of the species in the Paraná-Paraguay basin. Within the last decade, a diverse array of molecular genetic tools have become available for high-resolution genetic studies of population-level processes including microsatellites. In this study, AC and AG partial enriched library were constructed. Total DNA digested with DraI and SspI was size fractioned in 2% agarose gel. The 500-1000 bp DNA fragments excised and recovered by phenol/chloroform extraction were ligated to linkers and submitted to selection using biotin-labeled oligonucleotides. Enriched PCR products were ligated into the pGEM-T vector and transformed into competent E. coli cells. Positive colonies were screened by hybridization with AC and AG oligonucleotides using ECL detection system. Approximately, 120 AG colonies and 100 AC colonies were positive. The sequencing of the positive clones showed the efficiency of this method, once the majority of the sequences obtained showed microsatellites repeats with enough flanking region to design primers. Until now, twenty primers pairs were designed and preliminary results have shown that they exhibit a high degree of polymorphism, making them very useful for populational studies in this species.

23650: Studies on the growth and survival of fish larvae are important for both aquaculture and larval fish ecology as the larval stage is characterized by high mortality. Under natural conditions, the primary sources of mortality are starvation and predation. Under larvicultura conditions, problems with start-feeding are the major sources of mortality. Laboratory studies have shown that suboptimal prey concentrations during the first feeding usually result in slower growth and higher mortality. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the growth and survival of Mandi amarelo (Pimelodus maculatus) larvae in different prey concentrations under laboratory conditions. Larvae were reared on Artemia nauplii at 30, 110, 190, 270, 350, 430 and 510 prey/larvae/day. We used three 4 L rectangular plastic aquaria per experimental treatment. The aquaria was covered by opaque black plastic. Larvae were fed four times per day. They were cultured in salinity 1.5 ppt. There were differences (P < 0.05) in survival rates, total length, total weigth and biomass. Larvae reared at 190-270 prey/larvae/day were significantly larger than larvae reared at 30-110 prey/larvae/day. Although survival rate was affected by the concentration of Artemia nauplii, with an best average values of 22.9% at 30 and 110 prey/larvae/day and the lower values in the treatments of 190 and 270 (14.1%), 350, 430 and 510 (2.2%) prey/larvae/day. We can conclude that for larvae of mandi P. maculatus the best prey concentrations is at 30-110 prey/larvae/day. Although higher prey concentration incremented mortality of the larvae.
23651: The icththyofauna of 100 m long riffles of the mid course of the Batéia stream, Tocantins basin, was studied. Samples were carried out by electrofishing according to the three-removal method. Thirty-three fish species were registered and distributed in 4 orders and 9 families. Among these 33 species, 13 were considered occasional and 20 as truly residents in the studied locality; only 12 species (36%), of all sampled species, were taxonomically recognized but 21 are still under study. Therefore, we present results about the standard length of fishes that compose the ichthyofauna as well as a macro characterization of feeding habits of the resident species. Maximum, minimum and mean standard length of all sampled species was 10.5 cm, 2.6 cm and 5.6 cm ( + 2.2 cm SD) respectively, corroborating the proposition that the small length can be used as diagnostic parameter to characterize stream dwelling fishes. Among the 20 resident species, 2 (Cichlasoma araguaiensis and Astyanax sp.) were classified as omnivorous, 6 (Characidium sp.1, Characidium sp.2, Moenkausia sp., Knodus sp. and Astyanax gr. bimaculatus) as insectivorous, 9 (Hypostomus sp.1, Hypostomus sp.2, Hypostomus sp.3, Harttia punctata, Loricaria sp., Ancistrus minutus, Aspidoras sp.1, Aspidoras sp.2 and Hypostomus plecostomus) as algivorous/detritivorous, 2 (Knodus sp.3 and Creagrutus sp.) as herbivorous and 1 (Hoplias malabaricus) as piscivorous. Among the insectivorous ones, some are water column eaters and others are bentophagous; all algivorous/detritivorous are grazers and, among the herbivorous ones, Knodus is algivorous and Creagrutus is a seed consumer. Such results, confirm the high diversity and high trophic specialization registered in Tropical areas.

23652: Spatial-temporal variations on Bryconamericus microcephalus feeding habits were analysed. Bimonthly samples, were carried out at Andorinha stream (Ilha Grande – RJ, 23°05′and 23°15′S; 44°06′ and 44°23′W), in two stretches that differ in the canopy occurrence (open stretches – OS and closed stretches – CS). In order to recognize temporal variations in the feeding habits, we analyzed the stomach content according to dry and wet seasons. Spatial variations were analyzed according to the autochthonous and allochthonous items incidence from OS and CS specimens. For each sampled specimen data of standard length (SL, cm), total weight (WT, gr) and intestinal length (IL, cm) were registered. Stomachal content was analized through Numerical Frequency Method and T and contingency c2 tests were aplied. B. microcephalus is an insectivorous feeder, consuming both allochthonous and autochthonous items. Considering the spatial approach, we observed that the amount of allochthonous items is the same at OS and CS but autochthonous items predominate in the stomachs from OS (X2=5.04; p<0.025). According to a temporal approach, we observed that at OS autochthonous items predominate during wet season but, allochthonous items do not vary between both seasons (X2=5.19; p<0.025). At CS we did not register significant differences between seasons (X2=0.96; p>0.05). All the observed differences are referred to the incidence of autochthonous items. The high incidence of such items at OS, is a possible consequence of a high autochthonous productivity in the locality where sun incidence is higher and, the high values of autochthonous items, registered during wet season (summer), corroborate such proposition.

23653: Amphisbaenians are often included in the diets of Elapomorphinians, however, observations on natural diets during winter are rare. During the dry cold season of July 2002, we captured a juvenile Phalotris mertensi (SVL = 350 mm, tail length = 30 mm, body mass = 12,73g) in Rio Claro (22 ° 33 ′ S; 47 ° 32 ′ W) São Paulo State, southeastern Brazil. This snake was found foraging under the litter, in shaded area. After capture the animal reurgitated an Amphisbaena mertensi (SVL = 250 mm, tail length = 10 mm, body mass = 8,78g). The prey was recently ingested as evidenced by lack of decomposition. The animal was ingested head-first and was equal to 69% of the snake's body mass. P. mertensi is a fossorial snake that feeds on other animals with the same habits, and probably consumes virtually any available prey within the limits of its gape, particularly during winter months when prey is sparse. P. mertensi and A. mertensi were deposited at the collection of the Department of Zoology, UNESP/RC, SP, Brasil (DZRC 1003 and DZRC 1004), respectively.

23654: IBAMA / CETAS, wildlife sorting and destination center in Manaus, Amazonas, Brazil has been receiving apprehended, rescued or donated wild animals since 2000. The low numbers of animals received by CETAS could be due to a series of factors: the local population being unfamiliar with the activities of CETAS; up until September 2002 animals rescued by the fire department and other people were either taken to local zoos or released into the wild; local custom of eating all turtles regardless of their size and sometimes crocodiles as well; lack of adequate facilities to maintain reptiles; and not enough personnel to attend to all of the rescue and complaint calls. 23655: Pseudancistrus can be characterized by having small buccal teeth, papillate lips, poorly-mobile interopercular plates, snout covered by small bristles, unplated abdomen and reduced rictal barbels. Sexually mature males develop large odontodes on the border of snout and head and interopercular area. Currently, six valid species are known, with their distribution restricted to the Guyana Shield: Pseudancistrus barbatus (Valenciennes, 1840), type-species, from La Mana, French Guyana; P. depressus (Günther, 1868) from Suriname; P. guentheri (Regan, 1904) and P. nigrescens Eigenmann, 1912, from Guiana; P. coquenani (Steindachner, 1915) and P. orinoco (Isbrücker et al. 1988) from Venezuela. However, inventory lists have pointed out the presence of Pseudancistrus in the Brazilian Amazon. Preliminary analyses on large samples of Pseudancistrus from different drainages (Tapajós, Xingu, Mapuera, Trombetas, Uatumã, Mucajaí and Uraricoera), deposited at the INPA Fish Collection, have shown that new morphotypes are present in the Brazilian Amazon. At least four distinct color patterns have been already identified: plain dark (rios Mucajaí and Uraricoera), nigrescens-pattern; median-sized spots (rios Xingu and Tapajós), barbatus-pattern; minute-sized spots (rios Mapuera and Trombetas); and reticulate (rio Uatumã). Measurements are being used to compare the Brazilian material with Guiana specimens loaned from different collections (ANSP, MNHN, MHNG). Some measurements are showing sex-related differences among Uatumã specimens. The present work will be describing new Pseudancistrus species and surely expanding the genus current distribution.

23657: The Everglades of southern Florida, USA, are currently undergoing hydrologic restoration. This restoration will require tools to develop restoration targets and evaluate restoration success. The goal of our study was to develop this tool for evaluation of amphibian communities. We began by using new methods developed by the United States Geological Survey that use presence/absence data from several plots within a habitat (or along a hydrologic gradient in our study) to estimate detection probability and the proportion of a habitat occupied by a species (proportion area occupied or PAO). We chose sampling units randomly within each of six strata in Everglades National Park defined by the hydroperiod observed and habitat type defined by existing GIS vegetation layers. We conducted monthly vocalization and visual encounter surveys in a circular plot of 20m radius at each site. A total of 118 sites and 562 total surveys were conducted and 2201 individual amphibians were observed during the study. Individual species capture histories and corresponding covariates (habitat, hydroperiod, temperature, humidity) were used to estimate the proportion of each stratum occupied by a species and the detection probability. Given that species occupancy rates differed across hydroperiod gradients and that hydrology was the controlling factor of this difference, we identified combinations of species occupancy that formed a community of amphibians unique to a hydrologic/habitat stratum and developed an amphibian community index (ACI) for evaluating the success of restoration and management of Everglades amphibian communities. The communities identified will be used to develop hypotheses concerning the effects of restoration on local extinction and colonization, trends in the PAO of communities, and shifts in community structure. These hypotheses can then be tested and success evaluated during restoration. By providing a reliable and repeatable measure of community structure, the ACI will help managers reach scientifically defensible decisions.

23658: The Kihansi Spray Toad (Nectophrynoides asperginis) was first described in 1998 and is found only in a two-hectare region of spray-wetlands in the Udzungwa Escarpment of the Eastern Arc Mountains of Tanzania (Poynton et al. 1998). A captive breeding program for N. asperginis began in 2000 at the Bronx Zoo and the National Amphibian Conservation Center (NACC) at the Detroit Zoological Institute in an effort to conserve this endangered species. Little is known about the natural history and behavior of N. asperginis. However, it is known that females of this species give birth to live froglets. 23659: Fluvial stingrays (Myliobatiformes: Potamotrygonidae) are known for causing accidents in humans in the rivers of the Center-west and North regions of Brazil. Previous studies on those accidents attest that the stingrays are the main cause of damages to the man in those areas. This study intends to describe the reactions of Potamotrygon stingrays to different stimuli. 29 individuals (8 youngs, 12 males, 9 female) belonging to the Potamotrygon genus were collected with a net in Rio Javaes's sandy margins (near IIlha do Bananal), transported inside boxes with water. For the accomplishment of the stimulus, the animals were placed in a pool made with plastic blanket, with 1 m2 area and 10 cm deep. The aeration was made through battery air pumps. The disk of the animals was divided in 9 parts, 2 cranial-lateral, 1 cranial, 2 medial-lateral, 1 medial, 2 caudal-lateral and 1 caudal. For animals more than 16 cm wide, stimuli were applied with a stick with 8 cm wide extremity, for animals less then 16 cm wide the stick extremity measured 2.3 cm. 29 experiments were accomplished, in each one of them the 9 sections were stimulated and the respective reactions were registered (escape after the stimulus, attack with the sting, escape visually oriented before the stimulus, no reaction). After each stimulus a recovery period was given and the normalization of the movements of ventilation of the spiracles was observed, only then a new stimulus was accomplished. The results show that in 57% of the cases escape after the stimuli occurred, in 31% attack with the sting, 10% escaped after visualizing the stick and 2% showed no reaction. So we can say that the attack reactions happen mainly when the animal does not see that something is about to reach it, when the stimulus is given in the caudal and medium parts.

23661: It is estimated that the number of biological specimens in US museums and herbaria exceeds 750 million. In the vast majority of instances the collection location is recorded as a string of text and typically lacks geographic coordinates. We have developed a tool for interpreting descriptive locality text associated with natural history collections data, determining geographic coordinates and allowing the user to verify and correct the coordinates. Traditional methods for georeferencing collection data from text descriptions are tedious and time consuming, typically involving finding the locality on either a hardcopy or digital maps, plotting the locality, and determining the coordinates. Using our tool, GEOLocate, considerably reduces the time required to georeference locality information. It took 1 staff member approximately 1.5 years to georeference the 15,000 unique locality descriptions within the Tulane fish collection. Time trials with GEOLocate suggest that this job could have been accomplished in under 6 months.

23662: Anacondas (Eunectes murinus) show an amazing Sexual Size Dimorphism (SSD) where an adult female can be as much as 40 times larger the male. Former studies show that while females experience directional selection for large size, males are under stabilizing selection for an optimal size. At birth, males and females have the same size. What are the proximate reasons if the SSD? We analyze the diet of a sample of 77 animals (53 females, 24 males) opportunistically collected in the Venezuelan llanos for 9 years. An independent sample of 94 animals (56 males and 38 females) was analyzed recording wounds and scars present on their body. Anacondas show a diverse number of prey such as birds (51.9%), mammals (20.8%), and reptiles (27.3%). The only attempt to prey on fish was unsuccessful. The spiny body of the fish passed across esophagus (and skin) of the snake coming out of the body. Among adult individuals, females feed about evenly in all three taxa (28.6%, Birds; 33.3%, mammals; and 38.1%, reptiles) while males feed mostly on birds (72.2%) and reptiles (27.8%) dropping mammals completely from their diet. The difference in diet might be, at least partially, responsibly for the size differences since birds are especially lean due to the limitation that flight imposes on weight. Adult females show a significantly larger number of scars of several sizes compared with males (Chi square = 20.1 p < 0.001) and this difference cab be explained for the larger female size. Females seem to tackle larger, more nutritious, but more dangerous prey, that provide the energy needed for growth and reproduction.

23663: The species diversity of salamanders, genus Bolitoglossa, in South America has always been considered low when compared to Middle America. This difference has mainly been attributed to a relatively recent colonization of South America by bolitoglossine salamanders (late Miocene to late Pliocene). Additionally, Bolitoglossa altamazonica is reported for the first time from Venezuela. We conclude that the species diversity of salamanders in Venezuela, and likely in the rest of tropical South America, has been underestimated.

23664: The level of moisture in reptile nests can affect rates of water uptake by eggs and phenotypes of hatchlings. Previous studies have compared the effects of different moisture treatments that were held constant throughout incubation. Eggs within natural nests, however, experience fluctuating moisture regimes throughout embryonic development. We incubated eggs of the lizard Sceloporus undulatus in four treatments that had a mean water potential of – 450 kPa, but differed in their patterns of moisture fluctuations. Throughout incubation we measured water uptake by eggs and subsequent hatching success. After hatching we measured hatchling morphology, growth, and locomotor performance. Field hatchlings were collected and phenotypes measured to be used as a natural nest treatment. All hatchlings were marked and released at a field site in southern Florida to monitor growth and survivorship in the field. In general, water uptake by eggs was not affected by fluctuating moisture regimes. Hatching success did not vary among treatments despite short exposures of potentially lethal moisture levels. Moreover, hatchling phenotypes and subsequent survivorship in the field were not influenced by moisture fluctuations during incubation. Our laboratory-reared hatchlings, however, grew faster, ran slower, and had lower survivorship (when placed in the field) than hatchlings from natural nests. In our laboratory-reared hatchlings the effect of clutch greatly outweighed the effects of moisture fluctuations on hatchling phenotypes. Our results suggest that fluctuations in incubation moisture have minimal effects on embryonic development, hatchling phenotypes, and hatchling survivorship of S. undulatus.

23665: The importance of parasitism to mate choice has become increasingly apparent over the last 20 years. Most parasites are internal or cryptic, therefore choosers cannot directly measure parasite load and instead presumably indirectly assess its effect via the vigor of the host. I examined the effect of a large, obvious, external isopod parasite, Anilocra partiti, on the mating success of a fish with female choice and paternal egg care, the bicolor damselfish, Stegastes partitus. I experimentally parasitized 20 adult damselfish males and observed them for five months. Mating success of parasitized males decreased to zero immediately and remained low for three months. There was no initial difference in the courtship rates of experimental and control males, however. Some parasitized males did mate successfully during the final two months of surveys. Although the proportion of mated males was lower for parasitized than control males, the mean success of those mated males was the same for parasitized and control males. The proportion of eggs reared to hatching did not differ between groups, although their egg care behaviors did. The presence alone of these parasites appears to be sufficient to affect female mate choice, thereby reducing the mating success of the male hosts.

23666: Since Darwin, mechanisms that promote the formation of new species have been described and debated. During the modern synthesis, Dobzhansky and Mayr proposed that geographical isolation was a fundamental prerequisite for speciation. However, it was demonstrated that divergent natural selection could promote speciation even in the absence of complete isolation, a process that is now being called ecological speciation. The marine environment is an especially challenging medium in which to identify processes that lead to speciation, mainly due to the presence of a widely dispersing pelagic larval stage in most marine organisms and the lack of evident geographical barriers. This has created a long debated paradox about the mechanisms that generate biodiversity in an apparently high gene flow medium. Based on the geographic distribution of mitochondrial DNA lineages in three wrasse species (Halichoeres bivittatus, Halichoeres brasiliensis and Halichoeres radiatus), I challenge the widely accepted hypothesis of marine speciation driven by vicariance and distance, and present evidence for ecological speciation. In Halichoeres genetic homogeneity was observed between widely separated (3000 - 4200km) locations, indicating that, despite growing evidence for local larval retention in reef fishes, at least sporadic long distance dispersal occurs. However, deep genetic divergences were observed between apparently connected, geographically close locations (96 - 340km). Ecology brings an additional variable that seems to balance the co-occurrence of long distance dispersal and genetic breaks over short geographical distances, deep divergences were found between ecologically different locations, whereas genetic homogeneity is consistently maintained among environmentally similar locations, regardless of geographical distance. The pattern observed in this study indicates that ecology can be as important as geography in reef fish biogeography, and that a much clearer picture of the mechanisms that drive speciation in tropical marine systems will emerge when ecological characteristics are superimposed on the geographical landscape.

23667: Capture success is a key element of any attempt to sample or manipulate a population. All sampling methods depend on capture success and most indices of abundance make very restrictive assumptions about the constancy of capture success. Programs that attempt to control invasive species benefit from high capture success rates and may require capture rates that put all individuals in the population at risk of capture. A meta-analysis of 21 Brown Treesnake (Boiga irregularis) trapping experiments on Guam showed that a 24-fold variation in capture success occurred, and that the variation was not seasonal. We found that capture rate of large (SVL>900 mm) snakes was related (r2 = 0.26) to the abundance of lizard prey, but the effect size was relatively small. A four-fold increase in lizard abundance corresponded to about a two-fold reduction in capture success. Oddly, this phenomenon was not evident in juvenile snakes, perhaps because lizard prey are relatively superabundant for small snakes. All trappable snakes exhibited a strong (r2 = 0.90) and large (ca. 14-fold) response to abundance of rodent prey over the available range of snap-trap rodent abundances tested on Guam (0-8 captures per 100 trap- nights). For both prey types, the affected snakes were harder to capture in prey-rich environments. This may be related to the variation in capture success that we found to be associated with snake body condition: heavy snakes (double normal mass for a given SVL) were 8-fold harder to capture in traps than snakes that were 25% underweight. The large magnitude of these associations between prey abundance and capture success has strong implications for both population monitoring and invasive species control programs.

23668: The abundance, sizes distribution and feeding habit of two sciaenid fishes, Menticirrhus americanus and M. littoralis that occurs on beach sine samples at Mar Grosso and Cassino beach (32 S) is described. Prey-specific abundance is defined as the percentage a prey taxon comprises of all prey items in only those predators in which the actual prey occurs. 23669: There is a high diversity of activity patterns in the chorus and reproductive strategies of the amphibians, mainly between species in tropical regions. In this study we analyzed the reproductive period, reproductive efforts, occurrence of sexual size dimorphism, and the relation between body size and fecundity in the gravid females of Physalaemus nattereri and P. albonotatus, at the Serra da Bodoquena, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. These two species commonly inhabit open areas at the Serra da Bodoquena. The reproductive period was determined through the observation of males vocalizing, couples in amplexus, and tadpoles. The reproductive effort was measured as the ratio of weight of the gonad in relation to body weight. Physalaemus nattereri reproduced from October to January, while P. albonotatus reproduced from October to April. The males of P. nattereri (0.24) had invested more in reproduction than P. albonotatus (0.17), but the females of P. albonotatus (27.3) had a higher reproductive effort than P. nattereri (22.2). Physalaemus nattereri present sexual size dimorphism and corporal weight, where the females (51.3 mm; n = 42), on average, are larger than the males (47.3; n = 42; t = 7.22; p < 0.001). There is no sexual dimorphism for P. albonotatus (p > 0.05). Both species presented a significant relation between snout-vent length (SVL) and the number of mature eggs (P. nattereri; r2 = 0.31; p < 0.001 and P. albonotatus; r2 = 0.15; p = 0.03) and between the SVL and weight of the ovary (P. nattereri; r2 = 0,53; p < 0,001 and P. albonotatus; r2 = 0.34; p = 0.0009). Both species presented the same behavior of egg laying, but differences in attraction behavior were observed. Physalaemus nattereri is a species that engages in explosive reproduction, while P. albonotatus employs continuous reproduction. These species can adapt to several types of habitat due to behavioral and physiological features.

23670: Main life history characters include longevity, age to maturity, fecundity, etc. Its study through the phylogenetic hypothesis would suggest a better understanding on its evolution. Results shown that fecundity within the genus Sceloporus was conservative, however, in the oviparous S. aeneus and in the viviparous S. bicanthalis, two sibling species of the Scalaris clade, showed higher fecundity values independently of their parity mode. Higher values of reproductive effort are present in other species of the Scalaris clade but low lifespan of these two sibling species plays an important role to explain the evolution of this trait.

23671: Most of the studies on the maternal investment (relative clutch mass) in reptiles have been performed in lizards and snakes. In the last two decades numerous articles on crocodiles have been published, however just a few are dealing with to this topic. Previous studies established that Alligatorids invest larger reproductive effort to produce eggs, in contrast to Crocodylids. In the present study we compare different reproductive characteristics of two populations of Mexican crocodiles (Crocodylus acutus and Crocodylus moreletii) to species cited in previous studies and discuss the trends of the reproductive effort and its significance in the fitness of these populations. Results show similarities related to previous studies, except for the reproductive effort, which is smaller than in populations of the same species in other localities. Comparing both populations of Mexican crocodiles, we find significative differences in all the reproductive parameters, in fact, the relative clutch mass in C. moreletti, tends to diminish in relation to female total length and body mass, suggesting a smaller investment in the reproductive effort (and may be with the age), according to the trends showed by some species of lizards.
23672: The genus Rineloricaria is probably one of the most complex among the Loricariinae, with about 20 valid species, distributed from Panama in Central America to Buenos Aires Province, Argentina. In Argentina, the genus is represented by 2 species: R. lima and R. catamarcensis. In this paper we describe a new species of Rineloricaria from the Parana river and Uruguay river basins in Misiones and Entre Rios Provinces. The new species is distinguished from all others in the genus by its unique abdominal plating pattern, and by the following combination of characters: thin caudal peduncle (2.9-3.9 % of standard length); differently sized teeth cusps in both dentary and premaxilla; upper and lower caudal spines not developed as filaments, and snout tip with an oval area of naked skin. A key to the species of Rineloricaria in Argentina is provided.

23673: The geological history of the Indian subcontinent is marked by successive episodes of extensive isolation, which have provided ideal settings for the development of a unique floral and faunal diversity. By molecular phylogenetic analysis of a large set of ranid frog taxa from the Oriental realm, we show that four genera, now restricted to torrential habitats in the Western Ghats of India and the central highlands of Sri Lanka, represent remnants of an ancient diversity. None of the other biodiversity hotspots in the Oriental mainland was found to harbour an equivalent level of early divergence in this large amphibian group. By unceasingly providing favourable humid conditions, the subcontinent's southern mountain ranges have served as refugia for old lineages, and hence constitute a major reservoir of unique evolutionary history.

23674: We investigated the interactions of environmentally relevant concentrations of contaminants with ecological stressors. First, we examined the effects of 37-day embryo/larval exposure to the agrichemicals atrazine, carbaryl, endosulfan, and octylphenol (nominal concentrations: 4-400, 0.5-50, 0.1-10, 5-500 ppb, respectively) on streamside salamanders, Ambystoma barbouri, in the presence and absence of food. Significant differences from controls are reported and were only found at the highest agrichemical concentrations for all studies. Octylphenol delayed hatching, but none of the agrichemicals significantly affected embryo survival. However, larval survival was reduced by carbaryl, endosulfan, and octylphenol, and growth rates were reduced by endosulfan and octylphenol. Significantly more carbaryl, endosulfan, and octylphenol tanks had larvae with limb deformities. Endosulfan and octylphenol decreased larval activity, and atrazine- and endosulfan-treated salamanders exhibited skittishness in response to a vibration stimulus. Agrichemicals inhibited the decrease in refuge use and increase in activity stimulated by hunger. Further investigations on the effects of atrazine (actual concentrations: 0-200 ppb) and food abundance (limited and unlimited food) were conducted on A. barbouri from embryo to metamorphosis. In general, atrazine did not statistically interact with food abundance, and atrazine concentration was correlated positively with magnitude of effect. Atrazine decreased embryo survival and increased time to hatching and variation in hatching day. This greater hatching variation amplified size variation, facilitating larval cannibalism. Increasing atrazine concentrations decreased refuge use and activity. Both food restriction and atrazine reduced larval growth and metamorph size, despite atrazine having no effect on feeding rates. Food limitation delayed metamorphosis while atrazine shortened the larval period. Because reduced growth and smaller size at metamorphosis can lower terrestrial survival and lifetime reproduction, resource limitations and ecologically realistic concentrations of atrazine have the potential to cause or exacerbate amphibian declines in impacted systems. This research was funded by an EPA STAR grant (R829086).

23675: One of the most intriguing questions in evolutionary biology is the degree to which behavior is a necessary consequence of morphology. We explore this issue by examining phototactic behavior in epigean (eyed surface-dwelling) and troglomorphic (blind cave) forms of the teleost Astyanax fasciatus whose eyes were modified during embryogenesis by removing one or both lens vesicles from the epigean form or by transplanting the lens vesicle from an epigean fish into the optic cup of a blind cave form. Lens removal results in eye degeneration and blindness in adult epigean fish, whereas lens transplantation stimulates growth of the eye, inducing the development of optic tissues in the normally eyeless adult cavefish. Despite lacking functional eyes cavefish develop retinotectal projections and the latter are enhanced after an eye is induced by embryonic lens transplantation. Photoresponsiveness was examined by placing fish in an aquarium with one half illuminated and the other half dark and scoring their presence in the illuminated or dark half. Both the eyeless epigean fish and cave fish with induced eyes are indifferent to the illumination whereas the surface forms are scotophilic, suggesting that optic development and phototatic behavior are decoupled.

23676: Boa constrictor was introduced onto Cozumel Island, off the Yucatan peninsula, in 1971. The introduction of this predator has affected negatively the native species, many of them endemic to the island, on which the boa feed. It is important to know the areas of the island where boas live in and the vegetation types they use in order to develop management strategies to reduce boa's pressure on the native biota. Our objective in this study was to determine habitat use and preferences of Boa constrictor on Cozumel Island. We interpreted aerial photographs (February 2000; scale 1:75,000) from Cozumel in order to delimitate and quantify land cover types on the island. From July 2001 to February 2003 we used nocturnal transects on highway, diurnal transects by foot, intensive sampling plots and other boa encounters during field work, to estimate boa abundance and distribution on each land cover type. We found that 89% of Cozumel Island has natural vegetation. The dominant vegetation type is subdeciduous tropical forest, which is restricted to the central portion of Cozumel. Results show that boas are distributed throughout the island, in all vegetation types. They are more abundant, however, in the southeast portion of the island, where low tropical deciduous forest, mangrove, palm forest, and costal dune vegetation are distributed. These vegetation types are associated to fresh water ponds. There were no differences in abundance between sexes or seasons. These results are part of a monitoring system to assess management actions undertaken to control the boa population and to promote the conservation of Cozumel's native biota.

23677: We carried out nocturnal surveys of amphibians occurring at two ponds in Parque Nacional Yasuni, in the Ecuadorian Amazon. 23679: The evolution of diverse, bright color patterns in tropical reef fishes has posed a longstanding puzzle in behavioral ecology. Several approaches are discussed for studying the evolution and function of visual cues and visual perception. The Neotropical reef fish fauna, with closely related taxa in strikingly different visual environments in the eastern Pacific versus the Caribbean, is a unique comparative system for studying environmental effects on communication. Eastern Pacific fishes, from characteristically darker environments, are substantially darker than their close relatives in the Caribbean, indicating that background matching may play a role in the design of color patterns. Analysis of substitution rates in visual pigment genes in reef fishes suggests strong diversifying selection for spectral tuning, which may promote diversification of color patterns. Playback experiments using synthetic-animation techniques should prove useful in determining the communicative role of pattern elements.

23680: Ultrasonography has been used effectively to study reproduction in a variety of reptile species however its application to crocodilians has been relatively limited. In this study we present results from a pilot study testing the efficacy of using ultrasonography to monitor reproduction in the American Alligator, Alligator mississippiensis. Ultrasound results were then compared with hormone results. A total of 65 females were examined by ultrasonography during April, May and June. Ultrasound results were validated on a series of reproductive females (n = 14) necropsied for other studies. Vitellogenic follicles, recently ovulated eggs, fully developed well calcified eggs and atretic follicles were readily discernible with ultrasound in reproductively active females. Reproductive structures were observed in 27 females of which 20 were actively reproductive while 7 were non-reproductive, containing large atretic follicles. Oviducts were discernible in females with eggs. Ovarian state was also correlated with hormone levels. Ultrasonography can be used to accurately assess reproduction in wild populations and provide data to estimate the number of reproducing females in a given year.

23681: For many organisms, predation is a major source of mortality. Thus, mechanisms that effectively reduce the risk of predation would likely be under high selective pressure. Additionally, variation in response of an animal to a predator likely reflects the complex interaction of factors that influence predation risk. One of these factors is body size. Snakes are ideal models to investigate the effect of body size on behavioral variation because, unlike birds and mammals, morphology remains relatively constant with age but body size varies enormously. We examined variation in antipredator behavior within a cottonmouth (Agkistrodon piscivorus leucostoma) population. Behavioral responses to human induced predation risk were compared across a continuous scale of body size. Defensive responses significantly declined with increasing body size. After controlling for body size, no differences between the sexes were detected. Our data reveal an escalated progression of hierarchical defensive behaviors in smaller individuals. Possible factors contributing to the observed pattern are discussed.

23682: Many snakes hold the anterior part of their body erect as part of a defensive display, though this behavior is best known in cobras where the posture is often augmented by the hood. We explored the mechanics of this vertical posturing in cobras, and particularly the mechanics of defensive strikes initiated from the vertical posture. In particular we wanted to know how the vertical posture related to the snake’s center of gravity, and if defensive strikes from a vertical posture relied on pendular mechanics or a kinematic chain. We determined morphometric values, segmental centers of gravity, and whole body center of gravity for a variety of true cobras (Naja) and related genera. To look at variation in hooding behavior we compared the vertical posturing of juvenile Naja melanoleuca to that of adult Naja haje. The hooding behavior was documented using still photography, then with high-speed digital videography. The mechanics of the behavior were explored by determining the center of gravity for each specimen (using reaction boards) and by having the cobras hood and strike. Combining the data sets allowed us to track the displacement of the snake’s center of gravity during the vertical posture and ensuing defensive strikes, and to compare the kinematics to the predictions of pendular mechanics model. In the smaller cobras the pivot point between the vertical and horizontal portions of the body was consistently just anterior to the snake’s center of gravity. The need to support the vertical portion of the body constrained the horizontal portion, resulting in a reduced range of motion for ensuing strikes. Larger specimens held proportionately less of their body vertically and maximized the range of motion for defensive strikes. Though some of the cobras adopted almost vertical defense postures, the defensive strikes deviated from pendular mechanics and resembled kinematic chains.

23684: The Louisiana pine snake inhabits fire-maintained pine communities in eastern Texas and western Louisiana, typically associated with upland longleaf pine (Pinus palustris) ecosystems. Individuals are closely associated with Baird's pocket gopher Geomys breviceps burrow systems, using them for shelter, escape, and hibernation. In addition, pocket gophers are the primary prey of adult snakes. Telemetry studies indicate that snakes spend most of their time on ridges between intermittent drainages that typify the upland study sites, habitat that is characterized by well- drained, sandy soils. Compared to available habitat, they preferentially use habitat characterized by lower values for basal areas of canopy and midstory trees, number of total stems, % leaf litter, and number of logs; and higher numbers of pocket gopher mounds and greater percentage of herbaceous cover. These habitat measures are indicative of a more frequent and effective fire regime that maintains the open forest habitat with abundant and diverse herbaceous vegetation. Well-drained sandy soils and abundant herbaceous vegetation also provide suitable habitat for pocket gophers. Extensive surveys suggest that alteration of the fire regime resulting in encroachment of midstory vegetation and suppression of the herbaceous vegetation have detrimental impacts on pocket gophers and Louisiana pine snakes

23687: Mangrove, seagrass, and intertidal pool ecosystems are often associated with coral reef communities, and are thought to play a vital role in maintaining coral reef health. Proximity to shore and abundant resources, however, make reef-margin areas highly vulnerable to direct and indirect natural and anthropogenic stresses. In spite of their importance and fragile nature, faunal surveys of marginal habitats are often lacking or incomplete. We found 65 fish species from 28 different families and 2 classes during our preliminary survey of marginal habitats off Pulau Hoga, Indonesia during summer 2002. Our data represent a 2 to 3 fold increase in species richness over previously reported values for southeast Sulawesi intertidal habitats. Habitat characterization revealed relatively stable pH values, but highly variable temperature (23-35°C), salinity (34-47‰), and oxygen (12 to <1 ppm) levels dependent on tidal stage and time of day. We concluded that water depth, temperature, and oxygen are the major factors limiting fish distributions in marginal habitats. Predictably, all fishes collected in marginal habitats displayed critical thermal maxima (CTMax) above 38°C, and 50% had CTMaxima exceeding 40°C, making the Hoga fish fauna the largest assemblage of hyperthermal specialists studied to date. Studies of hypoxia effects on thermal tolerance of some gobies found that those confined to the harshest rockpool conditions possessed physiological adaptations that prevented loss of thermal tolerance at low oxygen levels, while others (mudskippers) showed marked reductions in CTMaxima with hypoxia and relied heavily on behavioral escape responses. A more complete understanding of fish diversity, marginal habitat conditions, and habitat-fish interactions will be necessary to effectively manage and preserve coral reef systems around Pulau Hoga and may also have applications in other Indonesian reefs.

23688: Despite the ecological and evolutionary importance of metamorphosis and complex life cycles (CLCs) in the Amphibia, simple life cycles (SLCs) and the loss of metamorphosis have evolved repeatedly in frogs, caecilians, and salamanders. Understanding the evolution of SLCs from the ancestral CLC is an evolutionary problem requiring the integration of ecology, development, and physiology. We present a survey of the taxonomic distribution the two types of SLC (paedomorphosis and direct development) in the Amphibia, review the life history theory and the ecological pressures that favor each types of SLC, and discuss the endocrine mechanisms that have been implicated thus far. We conclude with the suggestion of a simple conceptual model of the evolution of SLCs that considers both ultimate (evolutionary-ecological) and proximate (endocrinological-physiological) mechanisms to account for the loss of metamorphosis.

23689: Female preferences for male mating signals are often evaluated on single parameters in isolation or small suites of characters. 23692: Eastern Texas contains a diverse anuran fauna comprised of 13 common species representing 5 different families. Given the level of anuran diversity and the amount of seasonal variation in temperature and rainfall in our temperate climate we would expect to find a variety of breeding strategies. Many studies have used call censuses as indicators of anuran breeding activity since male anurans advertise for mates through vocalizations. We surveyed anuran calls nightly at eight ponds, six minutes per night, in eastern Texas from 1 January 2001 through 31 December 2002. Air temperatures and daily rainfall also were recorded for each of the sites. The breeding strategies we observed, based on call frequency only, were: 1) breed within a predictable season (summer) independent of local weather patterns; 2) breed opportunistically within a predictable season (summer) dependent on local rainfall; 3) breed opportunistically within a predictable season (winter) dependent on local temperature; 4) breed opportunistically dependent on local flood level rainfall events; 5) breed opportunistically year round dependent on local temperature in the winter and local rainfall in the summer.

23694: Ozone is a major component of urban air pollution. It is a respiratory irritant in mammals, and ozone inhalation causes inflammation of respiratory epithelial tissue and a shift to a shallow breathing pattern. Effects of ozone inhalation on other vertebrates are not known. Because amphibians have significant cutaneous respiratory gas exchange, a large portion of the respiratory surface may be directly exposed to air pollution. We exposed frogs (Eleutherodactylus coqui) to a range of ozone concentrations (0, 0.4, 0.8 ppm) and relative humidities (10, 60, 95%) for three hours and recorded buccal pumping and lung breath frequencies. Behavior of the frogs during exposure was observed and evaporative water loss (EWL) was measured. At lower relative humidities, EWL was high and frogs were less active, adopting water conservation postures. Onset of water conservation posture was earlier during exposure to ozone compared to control air, but the differences in behavior were statistically significant only at the intermediate RH (60%). At high RH, frogs remained active longer in ozone compared to controls. Ozone decreased breath ventilation and buccal pumping frequencies during exposures across all relative humidity conditions. Our results indicate that breathing patterns and activity of terrestrial frogs may be altered by exposure to oxidant air pollutants.

23695: The genus Chaetostoma is one of the most diverse loricariid genera, including 42 recognized nominal species. Results suggest that Chaetostoma is polyphyletic with four species closely related to the type species (C. loborhynchos), but eleven species placed in a well supported sister group, and three other species nested within the out-group genera. The genus Chaetostoma (sensu stricto) is diagnosed by the absence of contact between the supra-preopercle and the first infraorbital, and the presence of conspicuous round papillae on the naked snout. I propose this sister group to be considered a distinct genus, supported by three synapomorphies: an unexposed nuchal plate, the presence of a dermal keel on the posterior edge of the supraoccipital bone, and the presence of a laminar wall of skin along the dorsal internal border of the first pelvic ray. The available name for this genus is Hypocolpterus, previously considered a junior synonym of Chaetostoma. This kind of analysis is greatly necessary to diagnose highly diverse genera such as Chaetostoma, based on synapomorphies, before revisionary works are carried out.

23696: It is the goal of this study to examine the degree of genetic structure among seven populations of the spotted sand bass, Paralabrax maculatofacsiatus within the Southern California Bight. The degree of genetic variation will be investigated through the amplification and direct sequencing of the two internal transcribed spacers (ITS-1 and ITS-2) regions of the ribosomal DNA. The information gained from this investigation will enhance both our understanding of the level of genetic diversity among P. maculatofacsiatus populations as well as the level of connectivity among populations of marine of organisms with a pelagic dispersal phase.

23697: Psammobatis bergi and P. extenta are two sympatric skates commonly caught in the commercial bottom trawl fishery of Puerto Quequén (58°50′ W; 38°37′ S) Buenos Aires, Argentina. 23698: We have been monitoring the population dynamics of the toad Bufo granulosus for 15 years since 1986 on a peninsula in the Tapajós River, Village of Alter do Chão, Pará, Brazil (02°36′04″ S, 54°51′45″ W). 23701: Resilience could be measured as the sufficient time for communities to return to stable points after a disturbance. The Imboassica Lagoon (RJ, Brazil) was formed by the damming of the Imboassica River by a sand barrier. The artificial opening of the sand barrier of this lagoon in February, 2001 changed the abiotic and biotic conditions and affected the fish assemblage structure. Ten days after the opening, the sand barrier was naturally reestablished. With financial support of PELD-Site 5/CNPq and CAPES, abiotic variables and fish sampling were monthly taken from August 2000 to July 2002 in order to measure the time it took the fish community to return to initial conditions. Data were obtained from two sites: one near the sand barrier (A) and the other 1,300 m far the sand barrier in opposite direction (B). Fishes were captured with standardized gillnets and seines in both lagoon sites. A Canonical Correspondence Analysis (CCA) combining fish species abundance and abiotic variables pointed out salinity as the main influence (minimum 0.9 - maximum 28.7; VC = 87%) on the fish assemblage. A significant similarity of fish assemblage structure (Spearman, p < 0.05) was reached 11 and 14 months after disturbance in site A and B, respectively. Since these months the lagoon had reached low salinity values (< 5‰) and the abundance of Geophagus brasiliensis, Tilapia rendalli, Jenynsia multidentata and Poecilia vivipara , constant species before the disturbance, increased. Hoplias cf. malabaricus, a freshwater fish species sensitive to high salinity, reappeared. The shorter time that it took the site A to return to initial conditions suggests that the site B is less stable, as it is probably influenced by a local sewage input.

23702: The comparative study of the vaginal-cloacal region of different species of Squamata revealed a wide variation in the cloacal morphology. We describe the histology and morphology of this region in some species of the families Crotaphytidae, Phrynosomatidae, Polychrotidae, Liolaemidae, Tropiduridae, Xantusiidae, Gekkonidae, Teiidae, Scincidae, Anguidae, Xenosauridae and Colubridae. The cloacal cavities (urodaeum, coprodaeum and proctodaeum) were zoned by their histology. The presence or absence of the urinary bladder was determined in the examined species. 17 morphological characters were considered to be primary homology hypotheses. The character states were taken from our descriptions and from other descriptions in the literature. The characters were optimized over the topology derived from the parsimony analysis of the available morphological evidence, including the character described in this study. In accordance with the optimization results, the urodaeum bifid, the presence of glands in the anterior urodeaum and the place of junction of the urinary bladder to the anus, are synapomorphies of Squamata; the position of the anterior urodeal glands and the central junction of the vaginal tube inside the urodeaum are autapomorphies for Iguanidae. The presence of sperm storage structures in the utero-vaginal junction is not considered an informative phylogenetic character, since those structures are present in all other groups of Amniota. 23703: The rivers of Diamantina Plateau, central Bahia, Brazil, have since the XIX century been subject of exploitation of diamonds. In 1996, after complete exhaustion, mines were closed. During field expeditions in 1998 and 1999 in the Paraguaçu river basin, a new species of Geophagus, which is probably endemic to the region, was discovered. It is being described and the holotype is deposited at the UFRJ collection. Herein we describe aspects of its natural history in the São José river (sjo), the mined main channel, dragged and with no or bare riparian vegetation, and some non mined tributaries (tri). The species was dominant, considering its constancy, abundance and biomass. The analysis of stomach contents of 147 individuals revealed that it is invertivorous and feeds mainly on autochthonous resources. Diets varied significantly (p < 0.01) according to sampling site and size class, but not according to season. The niche width was neither spatially nor temporally different. Unlike other Geophagus species it presents a rather defined stomach and consumes little sediment, what suggests selectivity. The mean intestinal coefficient is 0.97, and the correlation between body and intestine lengths was positive (r = 0.903, p < 0.001). Underwater observations revealed aggregations in small groups and no apparent territorial defense. However, some isolated individuals with dark pigmentation on dorsal and pectoral fins showed an aggressive behavior related to parental care. Posterior dissection showed they were either mature or recently spent or spawned males and females, respectively. Although the highest mean gonadosomatic relation was registered in the rainy season in tri, the percentage of reproductive individuals was never lower than 70% in both locals and seasons. Feeding activity was high and the condition factor was not different between rivers or seasons. The species seems to be tolerant to the alterations previously caused by former diamond mining on the sjo bed and margins.

23705: Hylodes phyllodes and H. asper occur in syntopy in rocky streams of the Atlantic forest of southeastern Brazil. 23707: Past studies with the purpose of describing the activity period of Blennioidei species by using a naturalistic approach, classified them as diurnal, although few cronobiological studies had previosly been made for the group. In this paper the activity phase of Labrisomus nuchipinnis, Malacoctenus delalandii, Parablennius pilicornis and Scartela cristata has been observed under conditions of natural photoperiod. For this, a system of aquaria (12,5 l) was assembled with one individual per aquarium, a total of three individuals of each species. Direct observations of 15 minutes per hour samples, with flashes every two minutes, were undertaken during three days. In nocturnal observations two dim light bulbs were used. Results showed that all the species presented lower activity rates (0-4 moviments per hour), whereas P. pilicornis showed diurnal activity with an acrophase between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., and the other species presenting no rhythmic pattern of activity. Observer influence that occurred during the sampling phase was detected and eliminated from the data. Moreover, diverse environmental factors were suppressed in the laboratory, such as food availability, wave incidence, tides, besides the presence of predators and shelter. These may serve as zeitbeger, significant for cryptobiotic benthic species which inhabit the inter-tidal zone, such as the light/dark cycle (LD). Such factors may explain the low activity rate and absence of circadian rhythm. In another way, rhythmic plasticity may be responsible for the absence of this rhythm in Blennioidei, which would corroborate other studies that present evidence on the existence of plasticity in fishes. Additional studies should focus on the elucidation of the main zeitgebers, other than the LD cycle, that induce the expression of rhythm in fishes.

23708: A study of fish communities was undertaken in 4 reservoirs of upper Paraná river basin, southeastern Brazil: Furnas, Estreito, Marimbondo (Rio Grande), and Itumbiara (Rio Paranaíba). Samples were taken bimonthly, from July 1992 to June 1994, in 10 delimited reservoirs sites. Gill nets with mesh sizes between 3 and 20 cm (stretched measure) were used per site with an approximate soak time of 12 hours. Species richness, diversity, similarity and abundance (in number and biomass) were estimated for all sites. A total of 37,855 fishes were captured. Furnas and Estreito fish assemblages were dominated by non-piscivorous native species from small to medium size. Marimbondo had medium to large-sized exotic piscivorous species, and Itumbiara was characterized by native species of small to medium size, with equilibrium among piscivorous and non-piscivorous species. Among the reservoirs, the total bimonthly catches showed significant differences in abundance of individuals (P<0.05) but not in biomass. Some significant variations in abundance between years and dry/wet seasons were also observed. Species richness was lower in Furnas (40) and Estreito (25) than Marimbondo (48) and Itumbiara (50). This last reservoir also showed the highest diversity values for almost all indexes used. An altitudinal gradient between Furnas and Estreito (middle Rio Grande) with Marimbondo (lower Rio Grande) was observed. The lack of species from lower Rio Grande caused: the high similarity between Estreito and Furnas; the lower similarity of Estreito in relation to Marimbondo and Itumbiara; and the uniformity between Marimbondo and Itumbiara. The low similarity between Furnas and Marimbondo was caused by the lack of some small-sized species in Marimbondo reservoir. The introduced piscivorous species Cichla monoculus and Plagioscion squamosissimus probably played an important role in the change of ichthyofauna in Marimbondo, represented by: diversity loss, drastic decrease in abundance of some species and local extinction of others

23709: Preliminary data indicate that the main cause of mortality of leatherbacks in southern Brazilian waters is bycatch in fishing gear, so beach stranding may be a reflection of this problem. Since 1991, thirty one surveys (more than 7000 km) were carried out along the coast of Rio Grande do Sul state and part of Santa Catarina state to verify the presence of stranded marine animals. Once encountered, turtles were measured, photographed and sometimes transported to MOVI as part of its herpetological collection. A total of 46 individuals of D. coriacea was found in this period (CCL mean = 143.4, min = 116.0, max = 171.9; SCL mean = 132.3, min = 106.6, max = 158.0 cm; for a n = 20) of which 14 were females, 4 males and 28 not identified. These individuals were classified as mainly adults but also sub-adults. The frequency of records varied at months: 40.9% in January, 25% in November, 13% in December (Σ = 78.9%) and the rest in February, March, June and July. Another 83 records of stranded leatherbacks in this region since 1992 are listed in literature but there is possibility that some of these records are overlapping our data. Accurate estimates of turtles bycatch in southern Brazil are not available. We know that 18 leatherbacks were caught in five fishing travels monitored in one year interval between 2001/2002 so we obtain a preliminary CPUE calculation. Dermochelys coriacea is critically endangered worldwide and several populations have been depleted by industrial fishing activities. It's necessary to increase monitoring efforts to better understand how many leatherbacks are dying in south- western Atlantic fisheries.

23710: The structure of the snake community at Ferreira Penna Scientific Station, Para State, eastern Amazon, Brazil, was studied between 2001 and 2002 (90 days in total). Examinations of the relevant material from the collection at Museu Paraense Emilio Goeldi and fieldwork at the site allowed increasing the species list of the Station from forty to sixty-two, among in six families (Leptothiphlopidae, Aniliidae, Boidae, Colubridae, Elapidae and Viperidae). One colubrid species was recognized as new. During the fieldwork, three complementary methodologies were used: time-constrained search, pitfall traps with drift fences and occasional sighting, resulting in the record of 53 species (n=288). The occasional sighting was made with the help of local residents and resulted in 44 species records. Seventeen species were collected only occasionally and therefore were excluded from diversity analyses. The study area for time-constrained search and pitfall traps with drift fences has 50 hectares. The sampling effort of time-constrained search was 856 hour per man, resulting in 117 captures, with an average efficiency of one catch at each 7:30 hours. The less efficient method was pitfall traps with drift fences with only 22 captures in 3360 hours (one catch at each 153 hours). Five species were recorded only with time-constrained search and three species only with pitfall traps with drift fences. The most abundant species was Bothrops atrox (11.76%), Oxyrhopus melanogenys orientalis (8.82%), Dipsa catesbyi (8.08%), Chironius fuscus (7.35%), Bothrops brazilii (6.61%), Liophis reginae (6.61%), Leptodeira annulata (5.88%). The species accumulation curve did not reached asymptote, indicating that the inventory is still not complete. From the species of which the habit was observed, 24 (42.85%) were terrestrial, 10 (18.18%) semi-arboreous, 9 (16.07%) cryptozoic, 8 (14.54%) aquatic, 3 (5.45%)% arboreous and 1 (1.81%)% fossorial. Daily activity data were recorded for 52 species, 30 (57.69%) of which were strictly diurnal, 9 (17.31%) were strictly nocturnal and 13 (25.00%) showed diurnal and nocturnal activity. The commonest reproductive mode is oviparity. Juveniles and impregnate females were encountered over all the year.

23711: Dendrobatid frogs represent a family of neotropical anurans, some of which are characterized by bright aposematic coloration and the presence of alkaloids in dermal granular glands. Nearly 500 lipophilic alkaloids comprising 22 different structural classes have been detected in skin extracts from members of the family Dendrobatidae. Although it was previously thought that the frogs synthesized alkaloids themselves, evidence now indicates that alkaloids are sequestered unchanged into skin glands from alkaloid-containing arthropods. Alkaloid profiles are known to vary significantly in the species Dendrobates pumilio on Isla Bastimentos, Bocas del Toro Province, Panama. Although alkaloid variability has been shown to exist in this species, relatively few studies have specifically addressed the degree of spatial and temporal variation in alkaloid profiles. As part of a larger ongoing study, which in part is aimed to assess the level of alkaloid variation in dendrobatid frogs, alkaloid profiles were constructed for D. pumilio from five different sites on the northwestern coast of Isla Bastimentos in 2003 for comparison with the same sites examined in 2000. Furthermore, to accurately evaluate the extent of alkaloid variation within a single site, alkaloid profiles were created for individual frogs within these same five sites during 2003. From past data, we expect that alkaloid profiles will vary among all sites, both within and between years. In addition, we anticipate that alkaloid variation within a single site will be lower than that compared to variation among all sites. Temporal and spatial variation in populations of leaf-litter arthropods is known to exist in neotropical forests, and population sizes are known to vary seasonally. Given that diet is related to toxicity in dendrobatid frogs, then differences in alkaloid profiles on such small spatial and temporal scales may suggest that the availability of alkaloid-containing arthropod prey items is responsible for the variability observed in alkaloid profiles. Alkaloid profiles from individual frogs will be described and variation in alkaloids from five populations on the northwestern coast of Isla Bastimentos will be presented.
